links.outcome: AI performance disparities across age, sex, HIV status, and region of origin
links.effect: Insignificant performance disparities across age, sex, HIV status, and region of origin; sputum tests for suspected TB strongly correlated with model predictions.
links.quote: Subgroup analysis revealed insignificant performance disparities across age, sex, HIV status, and region of origin, with sputum tests for suspected TB showing a strong correlation with model predictions.

links.outcome: Missed findings in CXRs the AI labeled as without findings (false negative rate)
links.effect: Overall FNR 1.57% versus radiologists 1.85%, with 0% TB-FNR; AUC 98.51%. Some non-TB findings are still missed.
links.quote: AIRIS-TB was evaluated on over one million CXRs, achieving an AUC of 98.51% and overall false negative rate (FNR) of 1.57%, outperforming radiologists (1.85%) while maintaining a 0% TB-FNR.

unlisted_practices: Autonomous AI reporting of normal chest X-rays with deferral of abnormal cases to radiologists

screen.reason: The study evaluates a population-scale triage strategy where an AI model automates normal CXR reporting and defers only abnormal cases to radiologists, testing workflow impact, workload reduction, and demographic subgroup parity.

primary.practice: AI autonomous normal-triage with selective radiologist referral
